rawSources.locator: L297-L310, especially L302-L304: mackerel icefish are a white-blooded group found only in the Southern Ocean; they lack red oxygen-carrying haemoglobin in blood cells, making their blood colourless. L311 onward concerns other fish and does not broaden the claim.

literal.prompt: Какая особенность делает кровь антарктических белокровковых рыб бесцветной?

literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP identifies mackerel icefish as a white-blooded fish group found only in the Southern Ocean and says their blood is colourless because their blood cells lack red oxygen-carrying haemoglobin. This supports the stem and unique answer; the copper and plasma options are not stated as causes. Australian Antarctic Program L302-L304, especially L304.
literalGroups.locator: Australian Antarctic Program L302-L304, especially L304.

literalGroups.literal: У белокровковых рыб нет гемоглобина в клетках крови. Это красный пигмент, переносящий кислород; без него кровь бесцветна.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The source explicitly states the group lacks haemoglobin in blood cells and that this makes its blood colourless. The explanation keeps that scope and relation; it does not claim plasma transport or generalize to all vertebrates. Australian Antarctic Program L302-L304, especially L304.
literalGroups.locator: Australian Antarctic Program L302-L304, especially L304.

literalGroups.literal: Гемоглобин — красный пигмент, переносящий кислород в клетках крови, поэтому его избыток не объясняет бесцветность.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The source calls haemoglobin the red oxygen-carrying pigment in blood cells. Excess cannot explain colourlessness when the stated mechanism is absence. Australian Antarctic Program L302-L304, especially L304.
literalGroups.locator: Australian Antarctic Program L302-L304, especially L304.
